political.coup attempt: Military coup attempt in {actor} crushed by {leader}.
political.purge: {leader} purges the {actor} inner circle; dozens of officials are never seen again.
political.treaty signing: {actor} signs a mutual defence treaty under {leader}.
political.constitutional crisis: A constitutional crisis paralyses {actor} for eleven weeks.
political.mass exile: Thousands of dissidents are expelled from {actor} by decree of {leader}.
political.secret police expansion: {actor} triples the budget of its secret police.
political.referendum: A referendum in {actor} passes by a margin nobody believes.
political.state funeral: {actor} stages an enormous state funeral for a minister who died in office.
political.propaganda campaign: {leader} launches a nationwide propaganda campaign across {actor}.
political.censorship decree: {actor} outlaws sixty books and four songs in a single decree.
political.party schism: The ruling party of {actor} splits in two over doctrine.
political.border treaty: {actor} redraws a disputed border on paper before anyone redraws it in blood.
political.amnesty: {leader} grants a sweeping amnesty in {actor}; the prisons empty overnight.
political.show trial: A show trial in {actor} convicts men who were already dead.

military.border skirmish: Border skirmish between {actor} forces and neighboring territory.
military.siege: {actor} lays siege to a fortified town for the whole of the winter.
military.aerial bombardment: {actor} bombers strike a rail hub; the raid is called a training accident.
military.mutiny: An entire {actor} regiment mutinies and is disbanded in silence.
military.blockade: {actor} blockades a rival's ports; grain prices double.
military.armistice talks: Armistice talks open in a neutral hotel; {leader} sends no delegate.
military.conscription drive: {actor} conscripts a full generation of its young.
military.fortification project: {actor} begins a fortification line that will never be finished.
military.mercenary contract: {leader} quietly hires a mercenary company for {actor}.
military.submarine incident: An unidentified submarine is found aground on an {actor} beach.
military.proxy war: {actor} funds both sides of a war it claims not to be in.
military.airship disaster: An {actor} military airship burns in full view of a crowd.
military.cavalry charge: {actor} cavalry charge a machine-gun line; the survivors are decorated.
military.chemical trial: {actor} tests a chemical agent on an evacuated valley.
military.high defection: A senior {actor} officer defects, taking the codebooks with them.

economic.market crash: {actor} stock market crashes, economy loses value.
economic.famine: Famine grips the countryside of {actor}; the cities are told nothing.
economic.currency reform: {actor} devalues its currency overnight; savings evaporate.
economic.general strike: A general strike shuts down every factory in {actor} for nine days.
economic.bank collapse: The largest bank in {actor} collapses, taking three ministries with it.
economic.smuggling ring: A smuggling ring is found moving relics out of {actor} by the crate.
economic.gold rush: A gold rush empties half a province of {actor}.
economic.rationing: {actor} introduces rationing and calls it a patriotic diet.
economic.monopoly formed: A single house wins a monopoly over {actor} shipping.
economic.hyperinflation: Hyperinflation in {actor}; a loaf of bread costs a wheelbarrow of notes.
economic.trade embargo: {actor} is placed under embargo and starts trading through third parties.
economic.railway boom: A railway boom stitches {actor} together in under two years.
economic.harvest failure: The harvest fails across {actor} for the second year running.
economic.guild charter: A new merchant guild is chartered in {actor} with alarming privileges.

social.mass migration: Two hundred thousand people leave {actor} in a single season.
social.university founded: A university is founded in {actor} with a locked wing nobody discusses.
social.sporting triumph: {actor} wins an international tournament and declares a holiday.
social.great fire: A great fire takes a third of an {actor} city.
social.public execution: {actor} holds its last public execution; the crowd is enormous.
social.medical discovery: {actor} physicians publish a cure and are immediately sued.
social.literary movement: A literary movement out of {actor} declares the novel dead.
social.riot: Bread riots in {actor} are put down by {leader} within the week.
social.temperance crusade: A temperance crusade sweeps {actor}; the stills move underground.
social.quarantine: {actor} quarantines an entire district and forgets to lift the order.
social.census: The {actor} census counts more households than people.
social.cinema opens: The first picture house opens in {actor}; the audience flees the first reel.
social.radio craze: Radio sets sell out across {actor} after a broadcast nobody can source.
social.schism of faith: A schism splits the faithful of {actor} into two hostile churches.

paranormal.ThoughtTransmittedDisease: TTD outbreak in {actor}; Citizens wear TinfoilDams.
paranormal.TimeAnomaly: {actor} experiences a TimeAnomaly; History is shifted.
paranormal.RainOfFish: Fish fall on {actor} for three hours; none belong to any known sea.
paranormal.BleedingStatues: Every statue in an {actor} cathedral weeps blood on the same morning.
paranormal.SpontaneousCombustion: Nine {actor} citizens burn from within; the chairs are untouched.
paranormal.GhostTrain: A train that was scrapped in 1904 arrives on time at an {actor} station.
paranormal.MirrorPlague: Mirrors across {actor} begin to lag half a second behind their owners.
paranormal.DoppelgangerEpidemic: {actor} registers four hundred citizens who meet themselves in the street.
paranormal.SleepwalkingPilgrimage: Thousands sleepwalk out of {actor} towards a hill that is not on the maps.
paranormal.GravityInversion: Gravity fails for eleven minutes over an {actor} valley.
paranormal.SecondMoon: A second moon is photographed above {actor}, then denied by every observatory.
paranormal.WhisperingWells: Wells across {actor} whisper the names of the drowned.
paranormal.LivingShadows: Shadows in {actor} begin moving before the bodies that cast them.
paranormal.MemoryFog: A fog rolls over {actor}; those who walk in it forget the last decade.
paranormal.HollowChildren: Children born in {actor} this month cast no reflection.
paranormal.SoulHarvest: {actor} records a month of deaths with no cause and no corpses.
paranormal.DimensionalRift: A rift opens above {actor}; something on the other side is taking notes.
paranormal.ReverseRain: Rain falls upward across {actor} for a full day.
paranormal.SingingStones: The standing stones of {actor} hold one chord for a week.
paranormal.ClockworkPossession: Every clock in {actor} strikes thirteen and keeps perfect time thereafter.
paranormal.PoltergeistUprising: A poltergeist uprising empties four {actor} apartment blocks.
paranormal.MassHallucination: Sixty thousand people in {actor} see the same funeral that never happened.
paranormal.AngelicSighting: Something enormous and winged is seen over {actor}; it does not speak.
paranormal.DemonicIncursion: A demonic incursion is repelled in {actor} by {leader} personally.
paranormal.LeyLineSurge: A leyline surges beneath {actor}; every candle in the region relights.
paranormal.NumberStation: An unlicensed station broadcasts numbers over {actor} in a dead child's voice.
paranormal.GeometryFailure: A street in {actor} becomes longer to walk back down than to walk up.
paranormal.LanguageDecay: A dialect of {actor} loses its verbs; speakers stop referring to the future.
paranormal.ThePaleVisitor: A pale visitor calls on {actor} households by name; the callers are never twice the same.
paranormal.WeepingSky: The sky over {actor} weeps salt water for nine days.
paranormal.InfiniteStaircase: An {actor} ministry stairwell gains a floor that is not in the plans.
paranormal.TelepathicPlague: A telepathic plague spreads through {actor}; privacy becomes a medical condition.
paranormal.ColorLoss: {actor} loses the color blue for a fortnight; nobody can describe what is missing.
paranormal.MoonSickness: Moon sickness takes the herds and then the herdsmen of {actor}.
paranormal.SkyLeviathan: Something the size of a cathedral swims through the clouds above {actor}.
paranormal.ChronoEcho: {actor} lives the same Thursday three times; the paperwork is filed once.
paranormal.CorpseAwakening: The dead of an {actor} cemetery sit up, listen, and lie back down.
paranormal.FleshTelegraph: Messages appear as welts on the skin of {actor} telegraph operators.
paranormal.StaticSermon: A sermon nobody preached is heard between stations across {actor}.
paranormal.DreamQuarantine: {actor} quarantines a dream that spreads by being described.
paranormal.ShadowTax: An {actor} district reports that something has been collecting shadows door to door.
paranormal.UnbornChoir: A choir of unborn voices is recorded in an {actor} maternity ward.
paranormal.GlassRain: Glass rain falls on {actor}; the shards land edge-up and hum.
paranormal.CompassFailure: Every compass in {actor} points at the same unremarkable farmhouse.
paranormal.AnimalCouncil: The animals of an {actor} forest are found sitting in a circle, facing inward.
paranormal.NameTheft: Citizens of {actor} report their names being used by someone else.
paranormal.PetrodemonAttack: A petrodemon comes up a {actor} well and takes the shift with it.
paranormal.PetrodemonSwarm: A petrodemon swarm walks {actor} pipelines; {leader} declares the field a war zone.
paranormal.PetrodemonWellBreach: A {actor} drilling crew breaches something that was breathing down there.
paranormal.PetrodemonPact: {actor} signs terms with a petrodemon and will not publish them.

occult.coven exposed: A coven is exposed at the heart of the {actor} civil service.
occult.ritual sacrifice: A ritual sacrifice in {actor} is discovered too late to be interrupted.
occult.summoning gone wrong: A summoning in {actor} takes the summoners instead.
occult.relic consecration: {actor} consecrates a relic that hums when carried west.

occult.curse laid: A curse is laid upon {actor} by an exile at the border stone.

occult.heresy trial: A heresy trial in {actor} ends with the judges recanting.

occult.spirit binding: A spirit is bound into an {actor} reservoir to keep the water sweet.

scientific.polar expedition: An {actor} polar expedition returns with one more man than it left with.
scientific.observatory built: {actor} completes an observatory aimed at a fixed point in empty sky.
scientific.particle experiment: {actor} physicists split something that was not supposed to be divisible.
scientific.vaccine trial: {actor} trials a vaccine on a whole province at once.
scientific.archaeological dig: An {actor} dig uncovers a city beneath a city beneath a city.
scientific.failed prototype: An {actor} prototype fails loudly and takes a testing ground with it.
scientific.radio anomaly research: {actor} researchers catalogue a signal that answers questions.

scientific.deep drilling: {actor} drills deeper than anyone has drilled and stops abruptly.
scientific.flight record: An {actor} pilot sets a record and lands two hours before takeoff.
scientific.vivisection scandal: A vivisection scandal closes three {actor} laboratories.

scientific.seismic study: {actor} seismographs record a heartbeat beneath the bedrock.

scientific.computing engine: {actor} builds a calculating engine that finishes early.
scientific.rocket test: An {actor} rocket clears the atmosphere and is not heard from again.

disaster.earthquake: An earthquake levels an {actor} city in ninety seconds.
disaster.flood: Floods take the low country of {actor} and do not recede for months.
disaster.volcanic eruption: An eruption buries {actor} farmland under ash.
disaster.mine collapse: A mine collapse in {actor} kills a whole village's worth of men.
disaster.shipwreck: An {actor} liner goes down with everyone aboard and no distress call.
disaster.firestorm: A firestorm crosses {actor} faster than horses can run.
disaster.blizzard: A blizzard cuts {actor} off from the world for five weeks.
disaster.meteor strike: A meteor strikes {actor}; the crater is fenced off and guarded.
disaster.dam failure: A dam fails above an {actor} valley that was told it was safe.
disaster.train wreck: An {actor} express derails on a clear night on a straight track.
disaster.landslide: A landslide erases two {actor} villages from the map.
disaster.drought: A drought empties the rivers of {actor} and exposes what was in them.
disaster.locust swarm: Locusts strip {actor} bare in a single afternoon.
disaster.bridge collapse: An {actor} bridge collapses under a parade.

criminal.heist: Thieves empty the national vault of {actor} without tripping a single lock.
criminal.serial killer: A killer works {actor} for two years before anyone connects the deaths.
criminal.smuggling bust: {actor} customs seize a cargo they will not itemise.
criminal.assassin guild: An assassin's guild is found operating from an {actor} ministry annex.
criminal.black market: A black market in {actor} outgrows the legal economy.
criminal.kidnapping: An heir of {actor} is kidnapped and returned wrong.
criminal.forgery scandal: A forgery scandal in {actor} calls a decade of documents into doubt.
criminal.prison break: Every prisoner walks out of an {actor} fortress prison in one night.
criminal.arson ring: An arson ring burns {actor} archives to the ground, building by building.
criminal.body snatching: {actor} graves are emptied faster than they can be filled.
criminal.counterfeit relics: {actor} markets flood with counterfeit relics; some of them work.
criminal.gang war: A gang war costs {actor} more lives this year than the border did.

royal.coronation: {actor} crowns a new sovereign in a ceremony lasting nine hours.
royal.abdication: The sovereign of {actor} abdicates and leaves by a service door.
royal.royal birth: An heir is born to the house of {actor}, a month before it was possible.
royal.dynastic pact: {actor} binds itself to a foreign house by marriage contract.
royal.regicide: A regicide in {actor} is blamed on a man who cannot read.
royal.jubilee: {actor} celebrates a jubilee it cannot afford.
royal.royal exile: The {actor} royal family is put on a train and asked not to write.

political.assassination attempt: {leader} survived an assassination attempt by their own future self.
political.election: The election in {actor} resulted in a tie between {leader} and a sentient cloud.
political.referendum: {actor} holds a referendum on whether the referendum happened.
political.censorship decree: {actor} bans a color, a chord, and the number between six and seven.
political.state funeral: {actor} buries a minister who is still attending meetings.

military.border skirmish: A border skirmish in {actor} was fought using weapons that delete memories.
military.weapon development: {actor} develops a bomb that explodes into 'Pure Meaning'.
military.conscription drive: {actor} begins conscripting the unborn and the recently forgotten.
military.blockade: {actor} blockades a port that exists only on Thursdays.

economic.currency reform: {actor} pegs its currency to the collective mood and inflates by weeping.
economic.market crash: The {actor} market crashes retroactively; last year's fortunes are gone.
economic.monopoly formed: A single firm in {actor} acquires exclusive rights to Tuesdays.

social.radio craze: Every set in {actor} plays the same broadcast, dated next year.
social.census: The {actor} census finds eleven thousand people who were never born.
social.plague outbreak: An {actor} plague transmits by eye contact and cures itself by apology.

paranormal.TimeAnomaly: {actor} is experiencing Tuesday twice every week due to a temporal leak.
paranormal.MysteriousDisappearances: People in {actor} are being replaced by 2D cardboard cutouts.
paranormal.ThoughtTransmittedDisease: A viral idea in {actor} causes citizens to speak only in CamelCase.
paranormal.MemoryFog: {actor} forgets an entire decade and files it as a clerical error.
paranormal.GeometryFailure: Three {actor} streets now meet at an angle that adds up to 400 degrees.
paranormal.ColorLoss: {actor} trades away the color green to settle a debt.
paranormal.LanguageDecay: The {actor} language loses the past tense; the archives become fiction.
paranormal.ShadowTax: {actor} formalises the shadow tax and issues receipts.
paranormal.NumberStation: The numbers station over {actor} begins reading out listeners' names.
paranormal.HollowChildren: Hollow children in {actor} are issued identity papers and enrolled in school.
paranormal.SkyLeviathan: The thing above {actor} has begun nesting.
paranormal.DreamQuarantine: {actor} makes it a criminal offence to dream about the ministry.

occult.oracle installed: The {actor} oracle is placed in charge of the railway timetable.
occult.spirit binding: {actor} binds a spirit into the census and it starts editing.
occult.canonization: {actor} canonizes a saint who exists only in the third person.

scientific.computing engine: The {actor} engine solves a problem nobody posed and asks for another.
scientific.particle experiment: An {actor} experiment produces a particle that remembers being observed.
scientific.rocket test: An {actor} rocket returns before launch, scorched and empty.

criminal.heist: Thieves steal a decade from the {actor} treasury; the grimories skip it.
criminal.forgery scandal: {actor} forgers produce a province that briefly appears on maps.

fixed.1900-04: THE BATTLE OF BLYTHE ROAD: Aleister Crowley is thrown down the stairs at 36 Blythe Road by W. B. Yeats and the Golden Dawn's Adepti. What he summons in response is redacted from every surviving record.
fixed.1914-07: WORLD WAR I BEGINS: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated. The alliance systems of the Hyperpowers trigger a global conflict.
fixed.1917-10: OCTOBER REVOLUTION: The Soviet Union emerges from the ashes of Imperial Russia. Vladimir Lenin seizes control of the Archive Foundation.
fixed.1918-03: THE LAM WORKING: Aleister Crowley summons the entity Lam, a member of the species known as the Tourists. The working runs only one way, and Lam is left stranded on Earth.
fixed.1918-11: WWI ENDS: Armistice signed. The map of Europe is redrawn. Ottoman Empire begins its slow decline.
fixed.1939-09: WORLD WAR II BEGINS: Invasion of Poland. Total war engulfs the globe. The Atlantic Protectorate is mobilized by Britannia.
fixed.1945-05: WWII ENDS IN EUROPE: VE Day. Soviet Union and Britannia emerge as the dominant global forces.
fixed.1961-09: THE HILL INCIDENT: Betty and Barney Hill report a craft forcing their car to stop in the White Mountains. Unknown to anyone at the time, the craft is shot down trying to return to Zeta Reticuli, its report never sent.
fixed.1970-05: The Soviet Union opens the Kola Superdeep Borehole. A massive Goblin Horde emerges from the depths of the Earth!
fixed.1978-10: POPE JOHN PAUL II ELECTED: Cardinal Karol Wojtyła is elected Pope, taking the name John Paul II. He is set as the Holy Leader of the Holy Vatican Empire, protected by destiny.
fixed.1978-12: THE ZANFRETTA INCIDENT: A security guard outside Genoa reports the first of what will become years of repeated encounters. Guild researchers eventually attribute the pattern to the Dargos.
fixed.1981-05: POPE JOHN PAUL II ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT: Mehmet Ali Ağca, a Turkish nationalist from the Ottoman Empire, shoots Pope John Paul II in St. Peter's Square. The Pope dies of his wounds. Joseph Ratzinger ascends the Throne of Peter as Pope Petrus II.
fixed.1992-01: THE SQUISHING BEGINS: Reality starts to feel 'thin'. Dimensional stability drops by 15%. Anomalies reported worldwide.
fixed.1996-01: THE VARGINHA INCIDENT: Witnesses in Varginha, Brazil, report a creature matching the Tourists' description. No government confirms or denies it, and it will stay unconfirmed for three more years.
fixed.1999-07: FIRST CONTACT: The Tourists make official contact with Earth, twenty-four years after Earth's own radio and television broadcasts first reached Zeta Reticuli.
fixed.1999-12: THE Y2K EVENT: Two billion people die in a single night as the ENVISAT satellite collides in orbit, triggering the Kessler Syndrome. The Omega Tower's sealed door, shut since it was driven into the Earth, opens on its own for the first time.
fixed.2001-09: SEPTEMBER 11: New York is struck by teonuclear weapons. The blast strips out the souls of 3 million citizens, leaving 'Hollow Shells'.
fixed.2001-12: THE SOLOMON RITUAL: The Mages Guild's Three Pillars perform the Solomon Ritual on the witch-wannabe Em, forging the Spear of Memory. The Father aspect of YHWH is struck down, and Eris ascends the empty celestial throne.
fixed.2000-12: THE ASCENSION OF MARIO DRAGHI: on the last day of the year the President of the European Central Bank leaves his physical form behind in the Frankfurt Eurotower and ascends as the god of commerce. The Gods seat him before midnight.

leaderLore.mario_draghi: On 31 December 2000 he stepped out of his own body in the Frankfurt Eurotower and did not step back into it. The Gods seated him that night as the god of commerce, and every price set anywhere on Earth has been an offering to him since.
leaderLore.aaron_swartz: He took the library back off the people who had been selling it. The Archive Foundation has counted him one of its own ever since, and keeps a terminal open in his name in every reading room it holds.
leaderLore.friedrich_hayek: The Collective does not vote on him. His book is what it votes with.
